title: Top-k words
summary: Find the most frequent words in support tickets, with ties broken predictably.
prompt: You want the most common words in this week's support tickets. Write
def top_words(text: str, k: int, stopwords: set[str] | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, int]]
- A word is a run of letters, digits and apostrophes (`a-z`, `0-9`, `'`); everything else separates words.
Apostrophes at the start or end of a word are dropped (`'quoted'` -> `quoted`, but `can't` stays).
- Skip any word in `stopwords` (given in lowercase).
- Return up to `k` `(word, count)` pairs, most frequent first; **equal counts are ordered alphabetically**.
top_words("Login fails. Login page blank; login fails!", 2)
starter: def top_words(text: str, k: int, stopwords: set[str] | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
solution: def top_words(text: str, k: int, stopwords: set[str] | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
words = (w.strip("'") for w in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9']+", text.lower()))
counts = Counter(w for w in words if w and w not in skip)
template: top_words("Login fails. Login page blank; login fails!", 2))
Dojo.eq("ties are alphabetical", [("alpha", 2), ("beta", 2)], top_words("beta alpha beta alpha gamma", 2))
top_words("The export is broken and the CSV export is empty", 2, {"the", "is", "and", "broken", "empty"}))
Dojo.eq("apostrophes inside words stay, outer ones go", [("can't", 2), ("quoted", 1)],
Dojo.eq("k larger than the number of words", [("a", 1), ("b", 1)], top_words("b a", 10))
